messages.content: Create a single self-contained HTML file (no external libraries or CDNs) that animates the solar system on an HTML5 canvas: a glowing Sun at the center with at least 6 planets orbiting at different radii and speeds, smooth motion via requestAnimationFrame, on a dark starfield background. Output ONLY the HTML in one code block.

reason: canvas/svg=y, anim-driver=y, self-contained=y, orbital-trig=y, bodies(9|4)=y, html-doc=y

response.reasoning:
The user wants a single self-contained HTML file with an animated solar system on HTML5 canvas. No external libraries. Requirements: - Glowing Sun at center - At least 6 planets orbiting at different radii and speeds - Smooth motion via requestAnimationFrame - Dark starfield background - Output ONLY the HTML in one code block The user explicitly asked for output only HTML in one code block — so I should honor that and not add explanation after. Actually they said "Output ONLY the HTML in one code block." I'll follow that strictly — just the code block, no prose. That's an explicit user instruction that overrides my usual habit of adding a brief explanation. Now let me make this genuinely good, not a generic tutorial demo. Things I want to elevate: 1. **Sun**: layered radial gradients, animated corona (pulsing), maybe subtle noise/flares via rotating rays drawn with gradients. A warm white-hot core into deep orange/amber. Glow via multiple radial gradient passes and shadowBlur. 2. **Planets**: at least 6 — I'll do 8 (Mercury through Neptune) with distinct character: different colors, sizes, maybe Saturn with rings, Earth with a moon, subtle shading (day/night terminator facing the sun — draw a radial gradient offset toward the sun direction so the lit side faces the sun). That's a nice craft detail: each planet shaded with the light source direction computed from its angle. 3. **Orbits**: faint elliptical-ish circular orbit paths (subtle strokes), maybe slight eccentricity for visual interest? Keep circular but with varying radii. Orbit trails: fading arc trails behind planets would look alive — draw a gradient arc trailing each planet. That's a signature detail. 4. **Starfield**: static stars generated once (with varied brightness, size, slight color temperature), plus a few twinkling stars animated with sine. Maybe a faint milky-way band via a large soft gradient. Pre-render stars to an offscreen canvas for performance, and animate a subset of twinklers. 5. **Interaction**: the page should respond to input. Ideas: - Mouse move → subtle parallax of starfield layers and slight tilt of the whole system? Parallax on stars is easy and feels alive. - Hover a planet → tooltip with name + info? That requires hit-testing; doable: compute planet screen positions each frame, check distance to mouse, show a small label near the planet. Also could slow time on hover. - Click/drag → time control? A drag could scrub simulation speed. Or a small control: speed slider built in HTML. The user asked only canvas animation; adding minimal UI is fine but keep it tasteful. Maybe: scroll wheel adjusts simulation speed, click pauses/resumes? Keep it discoverable via a small hint line. I'll do: mousemove parallax + planet hover highlighting with a label; wheel to change time scale; click to pause/resume? Click might conflict with hover. Maybe spacebar pause too. Keep UI minimal: a small typographic header (title "Solar System" in a distinctive font — no Inter/Roboto; I can use a Google Font via CDN? The user said "no external libraries or CDNs". So no Google Fonts either. I'll use font stacks with distinctive system fonts: e.g., "Georgia" / "Iowan Old Style" serif for the title, or a monospace stack for labels — monospace gives an observatory/ephemeris feel. I'll use a serif display stack for the title and monospace for data readouts. That reads as authored. 6. **Signature moment**: comet! A comet on a highly eccentric elliptical orbit with a particle tail pointing away from the sun, appearing periodically. That's memorable. Tail particles emitted along path, drifting anti-sunward and fading. Also planet trails. Also asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter: a ring of small dots with varied radii/speeds — precomputed array, drawn as tiny points. Adds richness cheaply. 7. **Performance**: pre-render starfield to offscreen canvas; asteroid belt as precomputed positions updated per frame (or parametric angles — parametric is fine for ~200 asteroids: x = r*cos(a), a = a0 + t*speed). Drawing 200 tiny rects per frame is fine. 8. **Details**: - devicePixelRatio handling for crisp rendering. - resize handling. - Planets drawn with radial gradient offset toward sun: light side toward sun. Compute unit vector from planet to sun, offset gradient center by -r*0.4 in that direction... Actually lit side faces the sun, so gradient highlight center offset toward the sun. - Saturn ring: ellipse strokes rotated, drawn behind and in front (split drawing: back half behind planet, front half after). Simplify: draw ring as ellipse with rotation, then planet, then front arc of ring. Or just draw ring after planet with a slight transparency and clip? A decent approach: draw the full ring ellipse (two strokes), then draw planet, then redraw the lower half (front) of the ring. With rotation angle fixed, front half is the half with y > 0 in ring-local coords. I can use ctx.ellipse with startAngle 0 to PI for the front half. - Earth's moon: small dot orbiting Earth quickly. - Labels: on hover, show name + distance in AU + orbital period. Small monospace caption with a thin leader line. Nice ephemeris vibe. 9. **HUD**: minimal top-left title + subtitle; bottom-left a live readout: simulation speed, elapsed "years". Bottom-right hint: "scroll — time · hover — identify · space — pause". Keep it small, monospace, low-contrast but legible (I need decent contrast on dark bg — use ~#9aa or so, fine). Avoid gradients as decoration in UI — the canvas glow is physical light, that's fine and appropriate. UI chrome stays flat, typographic. Color scheme: deep space near-black (#050608 with slight blue), warm sun (white → #ffd27a → #ff8c3b), planets with muted natural palettes: Mercury gray, Venus pale gold, Earth blue-teal with white hint, Mars rust, Jupiter banded tan (I can draw bands! Jupiter with a few horizontal band strokes clipped to circle — nice craft), Saturn pale sand + rings, Uranus pale cyan, Neptune deep slate blue. Jupiter bands: clip to planet circle, draw 4-5 semi-transparent horizontal stripes with slight curve? Simple horizontal stripes clipped to circle look good enough, maybe with slight alpha variation. Add the Great Red Spot as a small dot. That elevates it. Planet shading: base radial gradient centered offset toward sun by 0.45r, from lit color to darkened color; plus a thin terminator. I'll compute per frame. Trails: for each planet, draw an arc from angle-Δ to angle with a stroke gradient? Canvas strokes can't have along-path gradients easily. Alternative: draw N short segments with decreasing alpha — e.g., 24 segments over trailing 0.5 rad, alpha fading. Cheap and looks great. Or use a conic-like trick: draw arcs with decreasing lineWidth/alpha in ~20 steps. Fine. Comet: elliptical orbit param: use Kepler-ish approximation — parametric ellipse with sun at focus. Simple approach: position via eccentric anomaly parametrization: x = a(cosE − e), y = b sinE, with speed varying via Kepler's second law approximated by dE/dt ∝ 1/r². I can integrate E each frame: E += k / r² * dt * timeScale. That gives realistic fast-at-perihelion behavior. Tail: emit particles each frame at comet position with velocity anti-sunward + slight spread, fade over life; render as small soft dots (radial gradient or just alpha circles with 'lighter' composite). Cap particle count (~300). Also a glowing coma around the nucleus. Comet only visible/active maybe always — it orbits with period ~ let it loop; when far, tail particles shrink. Emit rate proportional to 1/r² so tail only near sun. Time scale: wheel adjusts timeScale between 0 and say 8, default 1. Space toggles pause. Show speed in HUD as "×1.0". Parallax: stars in 2-3 layers; offset by mouse position * small factor; also the whole planetary system could shift very slightly (like 4px) — subtle. Also I can add slow ambient drift of star layer for life? Twinkle handles that. Milky way band: pre-render a wide diagonal soft gradient band with noise dots onto the starfield offscreen canvas — adds depth without cheap glow. Use a rotated linear gradient with low alpha plus denser tiny stars along the band. Let me structure the code: ```html Orrery — a living solar system
...
